# 2 Clement — Chapter 13 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Clement 13
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. So then, brothers, let us finally repent; let us be sober for the good; for we are full of much foolishness and wickedness. Let us wipe out our former sins from ourselves and, repenting from our souls, be saved.
2. And let us not be people-pleasers or wish to please only ourselves, but let us also please through our righteousness those outside, so that the Name may not be blasphemed on our account.
3. For the Lord says: "My name is continually blasphemed among all the nations," and again: "Woe to him because of whom my name is blasphemed." In what is it blasphemed? In that you do not do what I desire.
4. For when the Gentiles hear from our mouths the oracles of God, they marvel at their beauty and greatness; but then when they see that our deeds do not match our words, they turn from admiration to blasphemy, saying that it is a myth and deception.
5. For when they hear from us that God says: "It is no credit to you if you love those who love you, but this is a credit to you — if you love your enemies and those who hate you" — when they hear these things, they marvel at the extraordinary goodness; but when they see that we do not love even those who hate us but only those who love us, they laugh at us and the Name is blasphemed.
